newsitem.title: USA: Prosecution rests case in Oklahoma bomb trial.
newsitem.headline: Prosecution rests case in Oklahoma bomb trial.

text.p: The prosecution rested its case in the Oklahoma City bombing trial on Wednesday after calling more than 130 witnesses to tie defendant Timothy McVeigh to the worst attack on civilians in U.S. history.
"On behalf of the United States, we are pleased to announce that we rest," chief prosecutor Joseph Hartzler said in court.
McVeigh, a decorated Gulf War veteran, has pleaded not guilty to carrying out the April 19, 1995 attack on the Alfred P. Murrah federal building that killed 168 people.

The prosecution wrapped up its case in just 18 days, far more quickly than expected. Prosecutors called three final witnesses on Wednesday to drive home the human tragedy of the blast -- a survivor, a rescue worker and Fred Jordan, chief medical examiner for the state of Oklahoma, who identified many of the bombing victims.
Chief defense attorney Stephen Jones told reporters he planned to put his first witness on the stand on Thursday.

Prosecutors have portrayed McVeigh as a right-wing extremist who carried out the bombing to avenge the deaths of 80 Branch Davidian cult members in a confrontation with federal agents at Waco, Texas exactly two years earlier.
